posts.alt: A Santaluz Tuscan villa estate backyard at golden hour: sand stucco and stacked-stone walls under a clay barrel-tile roof, an arched loggia with a stacked-stone fireplace, linen lounge seating and a long wood table, a silver travertine terrace with a round concrete fire bowl, wide travertine steps down to a central lawn lined by two rows of olive trees over lavender and rosemary with low lights at their trunks; neighboring tile-roof estate homes sit close by on the right and across the rolling hills beyond
posts.hook: On an estate lot, the most expensive thing you can waste is the line from the door to the horizon.
posts.caption:
Big yards tend to get filled up instead of designed. A pool here, a kitchen there, a lawn wherever is left over.

This one is built on a single axis. Stand in the loggia by the fire and everything lines up in front of you: the travertine terrace, the fire bowl, the steps, a long lawn held between two rows of olive trees, then the hills. Lavender and rosemary soften the edges and smell like summer every time you walk through. At dusk, low lights at the base of each olive turn the allée into the path you take after dinner.

One line, held all the way to the view. That restraint is what makes a large property feel calm instead of busy.

The selections:
• Bedrosians silver travertine terrace & steps
• Eldorado Stone stacked-stone fireplace
• Warming Trends fire bowl
• olive allée, lavender & rosemary
• FX Luminaire uplighting

posts.style: Neighborhood · Driveway & Curb Appeal · The Ribbon Driveway
posts.alt: The front of an English Tudor storybook cottage in Kensington at golden hour, with red brick, cream stucco and dark half-timbering, a steep slate-grey roof and an arched wood front door; a ribbon driveway of two tumbled grey paver strips with a band of turf between them runs to a detached garage, a curved paver walk leads to the door between clipped boxwood, lavender and grasses, an olive tree and a large shade tree frame the house, low path lights line the walk, and neighboring Spanish Revival and Craftsman homes sit close by on both sides
posts.hook: Some houses don't need a new driveway. They need the one they were built with, done properly.
posts.caption:
Kensington's older homes were drawn for a narrower, quieter street. A full-width slab out front flattens all that character in one pour.

So this front goes back to the period: a ribbon driveway, two paver strips with a band of green between them, the way these lots were laid out a century ago. Tumbled pavers in a warm grey take the place of cracked concrete, and they'll look settled on day one. The walk curves to the arched door instead of running straight at it, between clipped boxwood and lavender, with low lights to carry you in after dark.

New materials, the house's original manners.

The selections:
• Belgard Mega-Arbel tumbled pavers, ribbon driveway & curved walk
• SYNLawn turf center band
• boxwood, lavender, olive & ornamental grasses
• FX Luminaire path lighting

Own an older home and want the front to match it? DM “DESIGN”.

posts.style: Drone Aerial · The Whole Yard, Working Together
posts.alt: A three-quarter drone aerial of a La Costa backyard at golden hour behind a contemporary two-story home with grey stucco and horizontal cedar cladding: a rectangular pool with a raised spa spilling in a sheer sheet, a light porcelain deck, a white louvered pergola over a lounge, a linear fire table, a turf lawn and a planting border of olive, agave, kangaroo paw and grasses along a tan block wall; neighboring two-story homes and their yards sit close on both sides, more homes step up the hill behind, and the ocean haze sits on the horizon
posts.hook: From up here you can see what most yards are missing: a plan.
posts.caption:
On a standard lot, every square foot is spoken for. The difference between crowded and generous is whether the pieces were placed together or one at a time.

From above, the logic is easy to read. The pool runs along the long side, so the lawn stays one clean, usable rectangle. The spa sits raised at the corner nearest the house, with a sheet of water that you hear from the lounge. The pergola covers the seating, not the whole patio, so the deck still gets winter sun. One long fire table bridges the lounge and the pool. Then a deep planted border along the wall softens the block and gives the neighbors' second stories something green to look down on.

Nothing fancy. Every piece just has a reason to be where it is.

The selections:
• Belgard Porcelain pool deck
• raised spa with sheer descent
• StruXure louvered pergola
• Warming Trends linear fire table
• SYNLawn turf · olive, agave, kangaroo paw & grasses

Want to see your yard laid out like this before anything is built? DM “DESIGN”.

posts.alt: A 4S Ranch family backyard at golden hour behind a tan stucco two-story home with a terracotta tile roof, set for a holiday dinner: a long linen-covered table with candles and place settings under a warm wood pergola strung with café lights, a stone-clad grill island beside it, a paver patio, potted citrus and rosemary, a turf lawn and a square stone fire pit with a seat wall in the foreground; neighboring two-story tile-roof homes sit right next door over tan block walls, with hills and more homes beyond
posts.hook: Happy Thanksgiving from all of us at San Diego Landscape Remodeling.
posts.caption:
In San Diego, the long table can usually go outside in late November. That's worth being grateful for.

Today we're thankful for the families who trust us with the place they gather, and for the crew and craftspeople who build it like it's their own. We hope your table is full today, inside or out.

If it does end up in the backyard, this is the kind of setup we love. A pergola wide enough for the whole table, with string lights for when dinner runs long. The grill a few steps away, so whoever's cooking is still part of the conversation. Turf for the kids between courses, and a fire pit waiting for dessert.

The selections:
• Trex Pergola with café string lights
• Eldorado Stone grill island with Lynx built-in grill
• Belgard Urbana paver patio
• SYNLawn turf
• Warming Trends fire pit with stone seat wall
• potted citrus & rosemary

When you're ready to plan next year's table outside, DM “DESIGN”.

posts.alt: A grown-in garden courtyard behind a single-story Encinitas coastal home with dark-stained vertical wood siding, a standing-seam metal roof and black-framed glass doors at golden hour: large warm-grey porcelain pavers with gravel joints wind through full drought-tolerant planting of olive, blue chalksticks, aloe, grasses and lomandra, a stone seat wall with a water spout falling into a copper bowl set in river stones, and bronze path lights; neighboring homes rise just beyond the wood fence with palms and eucalyptus over the rooftops
posts.hook: No Black Friday sale here. Just a promise that lasts a lot longer.
posts.caption:
Everyone is running a deal today. We'd rather tell you what happens after the project is finished.

Ten months after we complete a project, we come back. It's called the 10-Month Walk-Through, and it's part of every job at no charge. By then the garden has been through a full season of San Diego weather: the planting has filled in, the base has settled, the irrigation has run through summer heat and winter rain. So we walk all of it with you. Every joint, every light, every valve, every plant. Anything that isn't right gets made right.

A garden like this one doesn't peak on install day. It looks best a year in, which is exactly when we want to see it again.

The selections:
• Arterra large-format porcelain pavers with gravel joints
• Eldorado Stone ledgestone seat wall
• Bobe copper water bowl
• olive, blue chalksticks, aloe, lomandra & feather grass
• Kichler bronze path lighting

Want a firm that comes back to check its own work? DM “DESIGN”.
